summary: Five findings: four high and one medium. The accepted extraction labels its whole analytic base as library despite the missing positive-characteristic C_infinity package; sends the general Tate-algebra component to new work without identifying existing restricted-series code and the upstream owner; leaves the already-reviewed E14 convergence correction outside the authoritative statements; overstates Theorem 3.4 in its reader report; and omits three directly used papers from prerequisites. The shared DrinfeldModulesAndTModulesPartII destination and the ABP source route are otherwise appropriate. These findings concern the extraction, not new allegations of errors in the published paper.
checked: Independence: the extraction and its accepted review identify Claude Code sessions cc-7b31c4 and cc-2aeb03; neither was this Codex session codex-rtOQ9t. Read the issue, all 99 accepted items, both routes, all 20 prerequisites, the reader report, review JSON and review report. Compared the recorded sourceIssues with the affected items, especially E12, E14, E16, E23, E30, E31 and E33.

Read the complete 49-page published article, Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham, Zagier–Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic, Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), e18, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2024.18, at https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B9AC9CF28F90ABB495FDC43093D51E05/S2050508624000180a.pdf/zagierhoffmans_conjectures_in_positive_characteristic.pdf on 2026-10-01. Compared arXiv:2205.07165v2, particularly pp. 11–14, 18–23 and 48–58, for the longer algebraic proofs, binary relation and final small-weight arguments. The preprint's Sections 0–4 correspond to published Sections 1–5.

Checked the definitions of MZVs, AMZVs and ACMPLs; the AT_w and AS_w index restrictions; the s(w) and d(w) recurrences; the binary relation and reduction operators; weak and strong Brown theorems; dual t-motive matrices; ABP lifting; the lower-weight linear-independence criterion; the restricted normalized-period relation theorem; AZ_w = AL_w; the ordinary-character deduction of Theorem B; and the separately stated small-weight upper and lower bounds.

Read DrinfeldModulesAndTModules and the relevant FA and PS stage descriptions, with reviewed library-coverage entries DM.0, DM.2, DM.4, DM.6, DM.8, FA.2 and PS.9. Read upstream AdicSpaces Layer 0, particularly 0.4–0.5. Checked the proposed-roadmap directory and assembled atlas for competing ownership and the three missing supplier papers. Compared the Part II identifier and title with PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23; no second Part II is needed.

Read actual pinned declarations at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174: Polynomial, RatFunc, LaurentSeries, Polynomial.Monic, RatFunc.inftyValuation, RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty, IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange, PowerSeries.IsRestricted, PowerSeries.isRestricted_iff', PowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring, PowerSeries.gaussNorm and PowerSeries.gaussNorm_eq. Read Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369: TauCeti.PowerSeries.hasGaussNorm_of_isRestricted, exists_max_eq_gaussNorm_of_isRestricted and gaussNorm_mul_of_isRestricted. Searched both pinned trees for the characteristic-p completed algebraic closure and relevant function-field constructions; did not infer absence from names alone.

Checked that the 87 missing items are each routed exactly once, that all 11 planned items name existing stages, and that the one library item is the bundled base-field item. Checked the counterexample to the full-tuple convergence hypothesis and the q = 3, weight = 3 counterexample to the reader's unrestricted relation claim. No Lean compilation or supplier-proof closure is claimed; this is a section-16 extraction audit, not a blueprint implementation.

findings.claim: The whole base-field item is marked library although its statement includes C_infinity, its extended absolute value and the analytic completion package. Its four cited declarations supply polynomial rings, rational functions, Laurent series and monicity, not that package. Its own note acknowledges that C_infinity is not constructed. The resulting status omits a prerequisite needed by every Tate-algebra, period and convergence construction.
findings.evidence: Published Section 1.2.1 fixes K_infinity, C_infinity and the infinity valuation. At the Mathlib pin, Polynomial (Algebra/Polynomial/Basic.lean), RatFunc (FieldTheory/RatFunc/Defs.lean), LaurentSeries (RingTheory/LaurentSeries.lean) and Polynomial.Monic (Algebra/Polynomial/Degree/Defs.lean) do not construct the completed algebraic closure. FieldTheory/RatFunc/Valuation.lean DOES already define RatFunc.inftyValuation and RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty, so K_infinity must not be replanned from scratch. Analysis/Normed/Field/Dense.lean, IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange, requires CharZero for its complete target field. The reviewed AUDIT-20 entry for DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.2 explicitly lists the positive-characteristic C_infinity target as partial, with the missing normed-field/rank-one instance for K_infinity and the characteristic-zero restriction of the algebraic-closedness theorem.
findings.fix: Split the algebraic/valued rational-function setup from the analytic C_infinity package. Retain library status for the parts actually supplied, adding RatFunc.inftyValuation and RatFunc.CompletionAtInfty where applicable. Mark the C_infinity analytic package planned at DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.2, citing its reviewed partial coverage and the remaining norm, completion and embedding interfaces. Make the Part II import of that analytic base explicit and update the reader/counts. Any remaining prerequisite request belongs to DM.2, not a new duplicate roadmap.

findings.claim: The bundled missing item sends the general Tate algebra and Gauss norm, together with the genuinely specialized entire-series ring, to DrinfeldModulesAndTModulesPartII. It gives no reuse boundary for the restricted-series code already present or for the existing upstream Tate-algebra owner. The design therefore receives general analytic infrastructure as new Part II work.
findings.evidence: Published Section 3 defines the one-variable Tate algebra over C_infinity and separately the ring E with its finite coefficient-field condition. At the Mathlib pin, RingTheory/PowerSeries/Restricted.lean defines PowerSeries.IsRestricted and its subring; isRestricted_iff' identifies the condition as convergence of weighted coefficient norms to zero. At radius 1 this supplies the Tate-algebra carrier over an appropriate normed base. RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean defines PowerSeries.gaussNorm and proves gaussNorm_eq. At the Tau Ceti pin, TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean proves hasGaussNorm_of_isRestricted and gaussNorm_mul_of_isRestricted (positive radius, ultrametric normed ring, NormMulClass). Reviewed DM.4 coverage itself records Tate algebras as partly present. Upstream tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras, Sections 0.4–0.5, owns restricted power-series algebras, substitution/evaluation and their general topological interfaces.
findings.fix: Split the ordinary Tate-algebra/Gauss-norm component from E and the application-specific constructions. Record the available restricted-series carrier and norm results as library ingredients, and import remaining general Tate-algebra interfaces from the named upstream AdicSpaces layer. Keep E's coefficient-field finiteness condition, its uses in ABP, and any genuinely function-field-specific Frobenius/evaluation compatibility in the appropriate Drinfeld owner/Part II. Update the Part II brief to name that import. Do not claim that the existing carrier alone supplies the full Banach/entire-function package, and do not edit or re-plan the upstream roadmap.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24.result.json: PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/28.statement and /30.statement; subsequent ABP difference-system setup
findings.claim: The accepted E14 convergence correction remains in a note and the design brief, while item /28.statement still asserts that Psi is a matrix over the Tate algebra under only the full-tuple condition (2.1). Item /30.statement repeats that insufficient setup while forming tail series. The authoritative item statements therefore still permit undefined entries, despite the review already identifying the problem.
findings.evidence: Preprint Section 2.2.1, pp. 27–28 (published Section 3.2.1, pp. 21–22), defines every consecutive-subtuple series as an entry of Psi. For s = (q−1,q−1) and Q = (1,theta^(q+1)), the two normalized Gauss-norm ratios are c_1 = |theta|^(−q) and c_2 = |theta|. For i_1 > i_2 >= 0, their product is |theta|^(−q*q^i_1 + q^i_2), whose exponent is at most −q^(i_1+1) + q^(i_1−1), tending to minus infinity. Thus the printed full-tuple condition holds. But the i-th term of the suffix series L(q−1;theta^(q+1)) has Gauss norm |theta|^(q^i), so the terms do not tend to zero. This is the accepted extraction's existing E14 counterexample, independently checked here. Item /28.note and route 1 acknowledge it, but /28.statement and the tail-series setup in /30.statement do not include the correction.
findings.fix: Put the corrected convergence hypothesis directly into /28.statement and every setup that uses its prefix/tail series, including /30.statement and the ABP difference-system construction. A sufficient explicit choice is ||Q_j||_infinity < |theta|_infinity^(q*s_j/(q−1)) for every j; alternatively state and justify convergence conditions for all required consecutive subtuples. Preserve the printed full-tuple condition as historical source text linked to E14. State that the paper's intended gamma and gamma*H_s applications satisfy the strengthened condition. This is propagation of an accepted correction, not a new sourceIssue.

findings.claim: The reader says any nontrivial K-linear relation between ACMPL values forces (q−1) | w and is then unique. The theorem applies to a restricted family of normalized periods augmented by 1. The unrestricted assertion is false, even in weight three.
findings.evidence: Preprint Theorem 3.4, p. 35 (published Theorem 4.4, p. 30), restricts every index to J'_w, meaning q does not divide any component, and studies a + sum a_i*L_i(s_i;epsilon_i)(theta) = 0. Uniqueness is after setting a = 1; the periods contain gamma factors and division by the Carlitz period to weight w. Item /34 correctly retains these restrictions. In contrast, preprint Section 1.2's binary relation R_1 (p. 14), summed over d, gives Li(q) + (theta^q−theta)Li(1,q−1) = 0; the same identity is explicitly used on p. 22. For q = 3 this is a nontrivial homogeneous weight-three K-relation, although 2 does not divide 3. Li(3) is excluded from J'_3, which is precisely why there is no contradiction with the actual theorem.
findings.fix: Replace the reader sentence with the restricted augmented normalized-period statement: for indices in J'_w, a nontrivial relation involving 1 forces (q−1) | w and a nonzero constant coefficient, with uniqueness after that coefficient is normalized to 1. Explain that AS_w itself is independent and that general ACMPL relations are handled by reduction to AS_w. Preserve the correct item /34, including its gamma normalization and character qualifications; do not describe the full space of all ACMPL relations as one-dimensional.

findings.claim: The 20-entry prerequisites list omits three papers used directly by extracted results: Chang–Papanikolas–Yu (2019), Chen–Harada (2021), and the authors' separate Note on the Linear Independence of Alternating Multiple Zeta Values in Positive Characteristic. They are identified inside item locators/notes, but are not recorded for the later prerequisite batch. No separate coverage of these papers was found in the assembled atlas or proposed-roadmap catalogue.

Published Eq. (3.5), p. 23, cites [14, Proposition 2.12]: Chen–Harada, On lower bounds of the dimensions of multizeta values in positive characteristic, Documenta Mathematica 26 (2021), 537–559, DOI 10.4171/DM/821, arXiv:2012.00340. Published Section 5.4 and Proposition 5.13, pp. 45–47 (preprint Section 4.4 and Proposition 4.13, pp. 55–58), defer full details to [26] (preprint [25]): Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham, Note on the Linear Independence of Alternating Multiple Zeta Values in Positive Characteristic, Acta Mathematica Vietnamica 49 (2024), 485–521, DOI 10.1007/s40306-024-00554-4, HAL hal-04240841. The accepted extracted items themselves record these uses.
findings.fix: Add the three papers to prerequisites, with their public arXiv/HAL links and a why field naming the directly dependent items. Cross-link those citations from the relevant item notes and mention that the last paper supplies the small-weight proof details. Keep the existing cited-result items as black boxes at extraction level: section 16 does not require recursively extracting or proving their suppliers here.
